memory_update.text: ICHR should remain in the Layer 1B universe as a high-relevance underfollowed supplier for gas and chemical delivery subsystems used by semiconductor capital-equipment OEMs.
UCTT should remain in the Layer 1B universe as a second-order semiconductor equipment and contamination-control candidate tied to critical subsystems, parts, and ultra-high-purity cleaning services.

MKSI is larger than the preferred small/mid-cap hunting range but merits continued tracking because its vacuum, photonics, lasers, process-control, and specialty-chemicals exposure is strategically relevant to advanced-node and advanced-packaging workflows.
Need primary-source verification of named customer exposure, design-in duration, qualification cycles, and content-per-tool for ICHR, UCTT, and MKSI before any candidate can advance beyond Layer 1.

The most promising subnodes for the next pass are gas/chemical delivery, ultra-high-purity cleaning, vacuum/process control, specialty chemicals, precision components, and tool-specific qualified subsystems.

node: Semiconductor equipment, specialty materials, and qualification-gated tooling
summary: Expanded the semiconductor equipment/materials qualification node with a two-lane universe: ASML as the obvious reference bottleneck, plus underfollowed US-listed suppliers one or two layers beneath wafer-fab equipment OEMs. The strongest discovery candidates in this pass are ICHR and UCTT because they sit in gas/chemical delivery, critical subsystems, precision components, and ultra-high-purity cleaning services that are tied to fab-equipment qualification cycles but are less directly associated with AI than GPU, foundry, or lithography leaders. MKSI is larger and more visible, but still relevant because its vacuum, photonics, lasers, process-control, and specialty-chemical exposure maps cleanly into advanced semiconductor manufacturing and packaging.
